title: Affine base change of the proper flat coherent right adjoint
statement: Use schemes [def-pc-scheme], algebraic spaces and their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and the unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$ for objects with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Derived direct image is computed by K-injective resolutions, and derived tensor pullback by K-flat resolutions. A morphism of algebraic spaces is proper if it is separated, of finite type and universally closed; flatness and local finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts. Let $Y,Y^{\prime}$ be affine schemes over a scheme $S$, let $g:Y^{\prime}\to Y$ be any morphism and $f:X\to Y$ proper flat of finite presentation. Put $X^{\prime}=X\times_Y Y^{\prime}$ with $g^{\prime}:X^{\prime}\to X$ and $f^{\prime}:X^{\prime}\to Y^{\prime}$. Choose right adjoints $a_f,a_{f^{\prime}}$ to $Rf_*,Rf^{\prime}_*$ on $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$, with counits $\epsilon_f,\epsilon_{f^{\prime}}$. Let $\beta:Lg^*Rf_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf^{\prime}_*L(g^{\prime})^*$ be the canonical derived base-change map. Define $\alpha:L(g^{\prime})^*a_f\to a_{f^{\prime}}Lg^*$ by adjunction from $Lg^*\epsilon_f\circ\beta_{a_f}^{-1}$. For every $F\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$, $\alpha_F$ is an isomorphism and satisfies $\epsilon_{f^{\prime},Lg^*F}\circ Rf^{\prime}_*\alpha_F\circ\beta_{a_fF}=Lg^*\epsilon_{f,F}$.

proof.text: Write $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $Y'=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $h=g'$ and $t=\alpha_F$. Properness over an affine base makes $X$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated: finite type gives quasi-compactness and the diagonal is closed over the separated affine base. The flat pushforward base-change theorem gives quasi-coherence of the functor values and the isomorphisms $\beta_E$, and gives the same proper-flat-finite-presentation hypotheses for $f'$. The morphism $h$ is affine: on an affine scheme chart $U\to X$, its pullback is $U\times_Y Y'$, a fibre product of affines. By affine-pullback perfect detection it suffices to show that $R\operatorname{Hom}_{X'}(Lh^*P,t)$ is an isomorphism for every perfect $P$ on $X$; its cohomology gives exactly all the shifted Hom tests.

source.place: Tag 0E5I (lemma-more-base-change), first paragraph; Tag 0E4R, affine case.

proof.text: Fix such a perfect $P$. Put $H=R\operatorname{Hom}_X(P,a_fF)$ and $J=R\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_*P,F)$. The counit-induced adjunction gives $d:H\xrightarrow{\sim}J$ in $D(A)$. Flat affine perfect-Hom base change with $(P,Q)=(P,a_fF)$ gives $c:H\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B\xrightarrow{\sim}R\operatorname{Hom}_{X'}(Lh^*P,Lh^*a_fF)$. These results apply without boundedness of $F$ or $a_fF$. Thus the source of the desired Hom map is identified with $J\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B$.

The global Hom adjunction for $f'$ identifies the target with $R\operatorname{Hom}_{Y'}(Rf'_*Lh^*P,Lg^*F)$. Precomposition by $\beta_P$ identifies this with $R\operatorname{Hom}_{Y'}(Lg^*Rf_*P,Lg^*F)$. The perfect-sections theorem says $R\Gamma(X,P)$ is a perfect $A$-complex. Composition of derived direct images, applied to $f$ followed by the morphism from $(Y_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal O_Y)$ to the one-point ringed topos with ring $A$ (whose direct image is $\Gamma(Y,-)$), gives $R\Gamma(Y,Rf_*P)\cong R\Gamma(X,P)$ in $D(A)$. Since $Rf_*P\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$, under the affine etale module equivalence $a_A\dashv R\Gamma$ we get $Rf_*P\cong a_A(R\Gamma(X,P))$, so $Rf_*P$ is perfect on $Y$: a bounded finite-projective representative sheafifies to a bounded complex of summands of finite free sheaves. Apply flat affine perfect-Hom base change to the identity map $Y\to Y$, the perfect object $Rf_*P$ and $F$. Its canonical comparison $b:J\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B\to R\operatorname{Hom}_{Y'}(Lg^*Rf_*P,Lg^*F)$ is an isomorphism. This application uses flatness of the identity, so it puts no flatness restriction on $g$.

source.place: Tag 0E5I, right-hand-side paragraph and case (1); Tags 0CTM, 071Q, 0E4S.

proof.text: The definition of $t$ by adjunction already gives the trace equation. Indeed, for any $v:Q\to a_{f'}G$ its adjunct is $\epsilon_{f',G}\circ Rf'_*v$. Hence $\epsilon_{f',Lg^*F}\circ Rf'_*t=Lg^*\epsilon_{f,F}\circ\beta_{a_fF}^{-1}$. Composing with $\beta_{a_fF}$ gives exactly the equation in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0E5L (lemma-trace-map-and-base-change); direct calculation using the stated definition of alpha.

proof.text:
Check the map under these identifications. Let $T=R\operatorname{Hom}_{X'}(Lh^*P,t)$, and let $e$ be global Hom adjunction for $f'$ followed by precomposition with $\beta_P$. Then
$$e\circ T\circ c=b\circ(d\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B).$$
Both sides are $B$-linear extensions of maps from $H$. For the left side the underlying map pulls a Hom into $a_fF$ back by $h$, applies $t$, pushes forward by $f'$, composes with the counit, and precomposes with $\beta_P$. Naturality of $\beta$ moves that precomposition past the pushed-forward pullback Hom. The equation in step 4 replaces the resulting $\epsilon_{f'}\circ Rf'_*t\circ\beta_{a_fF}$ by $Lg^*\epsilon_f$. The composite is therefore: apply $Rf_*$, compose with $\epsilon_f$, then pull back by $g$. This is the underlying map of the right side, by the explicit constructions of $d$ and $b$. The canonical comparisons $c,b$ are the scalar extensions of these underlying pullback maps, so extension/restriction adjunction proves the displayed equality in $D(B)$, not just on degree-zero Homs. All four outside comparisons $e,c,b,d\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B$ are isomorphisms by steps 2 and 3; cancelling them makes $T$ an isomorphism. Step 1 now implies $t$ is an isomorphism. Together with step 4 this proves both assertions.
